messages.author: 7a97c986864bf6d6
messages.subject: Gamma reparametrization into mode / sd - Question on jacobian transformation
parts:
Hello, I'm loving Stan!

I have a question on jacobians within Stan.

A pattern is emerging on the sd sqrt(alpha/beta^2) and mode (alpha-1)/beta of a gamma distributed parameter.




Now I can reparametrize the gamma distribution for mode and sd but then I have to link mode and sd in, for example:

sd[n] ~ normal( ang_coeff * mode, sigma[n] );  equal to 

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
sqrt(alpha[n]/beta[n]^2) ~ normal(ang_coeff *  (alpha[n]-1)/beta[n], sigma);
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

if alpha and beta are vectors[N] how can adjust with the jacobian?


P.S. The plot above in terms of pure alpha and beta is 




Thanks

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Gamma reparametrization into mode / sd - Question on jacobian transformation
parts:
You need the Jacobian of the f:R^2 -> R^2 function

f(alpha, beta) = sqrt(alpha / beta^2), (alpha - 1) / beta

if you're going to declare alpha and beta as parameters and
put a prior on sqrt(alpha / beta^2) and (alpha - 1) / beta.
I'd also recommend sqrt(alpha) / beta as it does less arithmetic
and should also be more stable for small beta.

Alternatively, you can declare a parameter

vector[N] sqrt_alpha_over_beta;

and define

sqrt_alpha_over_beta ~ ...

and then derive the inverse of f to get alpha and beta back.
Then you won't need a Jacobian as you're putting the distribution
right on the parameter.

- Bob

messages.author: 7a97c986864bf6d6
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Gamma reparametrization into mode / sd - Question on jacobian transformation
parts:
Thanks Bob,

1)

just to make sure that is correct, I share a possible solution.

Considering that my priors will be

alpha ~ gamma( .., ..)
sqrt(alpha)/beta ~ normal( ang_coeff *  (alpha[n]-1)/beta[n], sigma )

a possible solution will be adjusting for Jacobian with two variables





for(n in 1:N) 
target += log(alpha[n] + 1) - log2 - 3*log(beta[n]) - 0.5 * log(alpha[n])

2)

it does not make sense to add 

beta ~ gamma( .., .. )

right? Or it could be done? In this case alpha and beta would have overlapping priors.

Thanks a lot!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Gamma reparametrization into mode / sd - Question on jacobian transformation
parts:
The formulas didn't come through.

You want to compute the Jacobian for

f : (alpha, beta) -> (alpha, sqrt(alpha) / beta)

Then you can put priors on alpha and on sqrt(alpha) / beta.
You probably wouldn't also want a prior on beta, but if
you include one, it just gets multiplied into the density (added
to the log density).

- Bob
